summary: Significant tail latency / eventual 504 on ultra-long multi-turn priming requests
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that for long multi-turn prompts (heavy priming + subsequent generation) the request appears to stream tokens normally for the first N% of the output, then slows dramatically and ultimately returns a 504 gateway timeout at the API layer after ~2 minutes. Impact: Blocking LexiAssist's nightly transcript exports and affecting user-facing features during batch runs. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod us-west, requests routed to cluster rwd-dedicated-14 using redwood-v2-large. Customer provided reproducible payload. Customer saw client disconnects and 504s intermittently starting 2026-03-07 22:00 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer example conversation JSON attached in ticket (primary system + 18 user turns, ~120k token priming).
2) Call /v1/generate with model=redwood-v2-large, max_tokens=150000, stream=true, prompt set to conversation payload.
3) Observe token streaming: initial 70-80% of expected tokens arrive with normal pacing; then throughput drops to <10 tokens/sec and finalization fails with 504 after ~120s.
4) Re-run on smaller priming (truncate older turns to keep priming <15k tokens) and observe normal completion within expected latency.
5) Re-run forcing model variant gptq-compat-8bit and observe similar tail slowdown but different failure timing.
logs: Customer client logs: last successful chunk at 2026-03-07T22:03:17Z, final connection reset at 2026-03-07T22:05:21Z, client sees HTTP 504.
API gateway logs (rwd-api-gw-prod): request_id=rq_0a9f2d, upstream backend returned error after 120.4s: 504 Gateway Timeout.

Serving runtime trace (rwd-dedicated-14): request_id=rq_0a9f2d, timeline: kernel_swap_attempt=2026-03-07T22:03:45Z, kv-evict-trigger=2026-03-07T22:03:46Z, batch-queue-length spike at 22:03:46Z -> saw 22s spike in processing of final shards.

Prometheus metrics: serving_token_throughput per-request shows drop from 220 tokens/s to <8 tokens/s at 22:03:46Z. GPU utilization remained 64% and not saturated; CPU usage on host rose from 12% -> 78% during tail.
No explicit OOM in dmesg; no preemption events recorded in cluster logs for that job window.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-08 09:00 - Initial triage by Support (Asha): reproduced with customer's payload on a staging dedicated node; confirmed tail slowdown and eventual API-level timeout when priming >100k tokens.

2026-03-08 11:20 - SRE (Diego): inspected runtime traces; observed unexpected KV cache eviction around the time throughput collapses. Hypothesis A: KV eviction causing repeated KV reloads and hitting scheduler/backpressure path, creating head-of-line blocking for the finalization stage.

2026-03-08 13:15 - Eng (Nina): ran an instrumented run with kv-cache debug enabled. Findings: when KV pages are evicted mid-request, runtime falls back to slower path that re-materializes key/value slices on CPU—this increases tail latency dramatically even though GPU isn't fully utilized.

2026-03-08 15:40 - Dev: tested workaround by bumping per-request KV retention for the customer's tenant (temporary config change) and saw successful completion for same payload with full throughput sustained; no 504 observed.

2026-03-09 10:05 - Additional check: scheduler queueing metrics show batch formation delay increased because the tail fragments were forced onto a low-priority host due to autoscaler hinting. Hypothesis B: interaction between KV eviction and autoscaler placement created a slow-path placement (fallback CPU) causing the long tail.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: increased per-tenant KV retention window for LexiAssist in dedicated pool and disabled aggressive eviction for active requests. Customer confirmed two successful runs on 2026-03-09 without 504. Long-term fix: engineering to modify KV eviction logic to avoid mid-request eviction and add guardrail to prevent placement onto low-priority CPU fallback during active streaming. Follow-up PRs: gh#redwood/serving-runtime#4821 (KV eviction fix) and gh#redwood/scheduler#4899 (placement guard). Rolling ETA: patch landing in canary 2026-03-15, full rollout after verification. Ticket remains open until patch is in prod and monitored for 72h.
